name: Purpose Sport
tagline: Site for a basketball player management agency, built as a talent catalog for clubs and partners
role: For an agency representing basketball players, I built a showcase that explains the mission in a few screens, then presents each player like a recruitment dossier (career, awards, highlight video). Bilingual Next.js one-pager, indexed from launch (metadata, Search Console, auto sitemap), with Analytics and Jest tests per section. V1 in three days, then a full art-direction rewrite. 61 commits, live on purpose-sport.com.

meta.title: Purpose Sport · Case study
meta.description: Basketball management agency showcase: player catalog, video, SEO and Jest tests.

paragraphs: A sports management agency sells trust. A sporting director must quickly see who it represents and why to trust it. Without a credible site it depends on word of mouth and social media.
Core need: the players. A recruiter wants position, career, awards and game footage, fast, without ten tabs.
The site also had to be findable: name on Google, clean social previews.
V1 in three days (16-18/01/2025): nav, hero, about, player accordion, contact. Goal: something concrete to discuss.

23/03/2025: hard call to delete everything and restart. The accordion hid players. Rebuild around a central Players section (card + video) and objective cards, then new art direction in early April. Restarting cost less than bending the old code.
Content separated from code: players in typed data/data.ts. Adding a player is an entry. Jest tests what users see (active player, pagination, player), not implementation details.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: Audiences: club recruiters and sporting directors, partners/sponsors, then players and families.
One page, six blocks: Hero, About, Objectives, Players, Contact, Footer. Horizontal nav follows scroll and hides near the form.
Out of v1: player area, per-player indexable pages, live stats, back office. Content edited in code, reasonable for ~10 profiles.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Layout: full SEO (OG, Twitter, canonical, robots, Search Console, manifest), three next/font faces, Analytics, i18n and scroll providers.
Players: active card (career, awards, video) + paginated list of 6. react-player via dynamic ssr:false for light first paint and no hydration issues.
Contact: five a11y-labeled fields via Web3Forms. No database: players, videos and translations ship with the site. Sitemap/robots regenerated postbuild.
bullets: ~5–6k lines including player data and i18n

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: Restart at the right time. March 2025 V1 worked but contradicted the goal. Delete and rebuild in three days rather than pile patches.
Video without tanking the page: player loaded on demand client-side only.
Scroll-aware nav via shared IntersectionObserver; navbar hides when the form fills the viewport.
bullets: RSC CVE fix on 23/12/2025 then release 1.0.0

execution.title: Delivery and next steps
paragraphs: 16-18/01/2025: V1. 13/03: animations, skeletons, mobile. 23-25/03: rewrite, objectives, Players+video, Husky, Jest. 04-10/04: desktop/mobile, Analytics, art direction, Search Console, sitemap. 23/12/2025: security fix and release 1.0.0.
Numbers: 61 commits on 13 active days, 6 tests, 20 components, 11 profiles, 2 languages, 1 full rewrite.

Honesty: early-2025 project. Larger components than I write today, videos in the repo, unfinished locale detection. Next: split sections, host videos elsewhere with posters, visible form failure states, CI, per-player indexable pages.
